column2: The station just cleared out some inventory.
It was a mess. The crates are still sealed.
Interested?
My name was on the layoff list.
No severance? I'll make my own.
600 credits.
I heard you can handle this stuff.
This crate was delivered to the wrong place.
Oh well.
I signed for it myself.
My supervisor says interns should take ownership.
I always treated the company like family.
So I took a little something from the family.
Seems fair, right?
I heard the company was restructuring.
I did some digging,
and found out I was on the list.
So I decided to help restructure the inventory first.
This came from the Security Department.
I don't want to know what you'll do with it.
Let's just make this quick.
Found it on patrol. It isn't in the logs.
I don't want to spend the night with it.
Let's trade. I need to get back.
I make sure nothing gets stolen from the warehouse.
Now it's in my hands.
Call it a write-off.
This shipment came straight out of the Security Department.
Command says there are classified documents inside.
You won't regret buying it.
The evidence-room seals are still intact.
Someone will start asking questions if it stays there.
Make it disappear for me.
You know what evidence preservation means?
Before evidence can disappear,
you make sure it never appears in any record.
Don't look at me like that. I'm speaking hypothetically.
Relax.
This is a routine security inspection.
*Winks at you*
Three people knew this shipment existed.
Now there are only two.
I hope you can keep it that way.
You heard?
There was a complicated theft in the lower district.
They have a suspect and a victim.
All that's missing is the stolen property.
The med bay just got a new shipment.
This crate isn't on the manifest.
600 credits, and it's yours.
A doctor owed me money. This covered the debt.
I have no use for this stuff.
You should think it over.
The chief says medical supplies should go to those in need.
You probably need them more than we do.
So I brought them to you.
The med bay's building a new wing,
but the procurement budget ran out before construction began.
Funny how that happens.
This is a reinforced supply crate from the foundry.
Inventory got messy. I don't want to ask questions.
Give me a little for the trouble and it's yours.
There was an extra crate in the factory warehouse. No one claimed it.
Want to take it?
Engineering's materials crate.
The foreman said to take it instead of my wages.
No idea where he got it.
After a few rounds of subcontracting, the project landed with me.
I'm asking half of what they did.
Don't ask where the cash flow came from.
People in the lower district have started talking about you.
I can spread the word upstairs. The goods are more valuable there, and much hotter.
I'll need 1,000 credits to grease a few palms.
Word in the upper district doesn't come cheap.
All right.
Someone from upstairs should be looking for you in a day or two.
Keep an eye out.
Call me if you need another introduction.
No rush.
Save up first.
Call me when there's business to discuss.
Have you heard?
A batch of valuable lost property was stolen from the upper district.
If you find any of it and want to sell,
give me a call. I can find you a buyer.
I hear you have something I've been looking for.
Let's make this quick.
Keep it quiet. I know you've got the goods.
Lovely weather today, isn't it?
*Winks at you*
This shipment was never meant for a regular warehouse.
The purchase order says it's for special use.
I'm sure you know what to do with it.
I've worked in logistics for over ten years.
I've seen plenty go into the warehouse and plenty come out.
But I can't handle this shipment.
These supplies were reserved for the premium allocation list.
The people on it don't know their allocation was canceled yet.
You can hold on to it for them.
The company put special assets under restricted handling.
I handle the restrictions. Someone else handles the assets.
Now I've taken care of both.
A toolbox from an upper-district engineering crew.
What's inside is worth more than I need. 1,500 credits. Deal?
Someone gave me an engineering crate as collateral.
I'd rather have cash. Take it for 1,500.
Supplies from an upper-district medical ward.
Don't ask where they came from.
Take a look.
I just finished a private operation.
There were plenty of supplies left over.
These should have gone through loss accounting.
Don't ask questions.
These supplies were seized during an internal security inspection.
The inspection team has been disbanded.
As for why the supplies are still here...
Security supplies from the upper district.
I've never seen them touch a gun, though.
So I bought a 3D-printed gun at the pawn shop next door
and put it in the warehouse.
This was meant for a special operations team.
The operation was canceled, but the budget wasn't.
You know how it is. Every budget needs somewhere to go.
This crate came from the Security Department evidence room.
The seals haven't even been broken.
Once you take it, it's no longer my problem.
Some evidence shouldn't stay in storage.
I just make sure the crate leaves.
These supplies were marked as classified evidence.
Three investigators were supposed to guard them.
Now I'm the only one left.
